tasks.contextSummary: A helical spring within its Hooke-law region; blank axes supplied.
solutionStructure: Draw a straight positive-gradient line through the origin.

criteria.rule: Appropriate paired physical quantities on axes; orientation does not matter.
Straight increasing line over the Hooke-law region.

acceptableAlternatives: The scheme permits elongation or distance/length stretched for extension, and force/load/weight for the loading quantity.
A total-length axis can receive full credit with the correct non-zero length intercept.
A curve beyond a clearly identified proportional limit is permitted. Units are ignored for this sketch.
dependencies: Interpret the origin criterion with the chosen axis quantity: total length is not extension.

commonErrors.description: Putting total length through the origin
Substituting elastic limit for an identified proportional limit

requiredKnowledge: Resultant force equals mass times acceleration
tasks.contextSummary: Same released object; mass 0.20 kg; uses resultant from the preceding part.
solutionStructure: Substitute F = ma using 1.2 N and 0.20 kg.

criteria.rule: Substitution into resultant force = mass × acceleration.
Consistent numerical evaluation, 6.0 m/s² for the correct previous value.

acceptableAlternatives: The scheme permits error carried forward from 5.b.i.
dependencies: Evaluate the working using the candidate’s earlier resultant where the scheme allows ECF.
The scheme specifies a one-mark loss for a power-of-ten error; do not multiply penalties across repeated use of that error.

tasks.assessmentObjectiveStatus: No official per-leaf AO allocation inspected; not inferred as authoritative.
tasks.contextSummary: From release below equilibrium until the first return to the initial equilibrium position.
solutionStructure: Spring extension and upward spring force decrease while weight stays constant.
The upward resultant therefore falls to zero at equilibrium.

criteria.rule: Acceleration decreases to zero; “decelerates” is not the requested statement.
Any two distinct valid supports: reduced extension, reduced upward spring force, unchanged weight, reduced resultant reaching zero.

acceptableAlternatives: Less stretched can express reduced extension.
Balanced forces is suitable if clearly limited to the equilibrium endpoint.
dependencies: The support alternatives have a two-mark group cap, not four available marks.
Do not equate falling acceleration magnitude with falling speed during this interval.

commonErrors.description: Calling the upward-moving object slower because its acceleration falls
Claiming forces balance throughout the path

requiredKnowledge: Instantaneous gradient of a curved velocity-time graph
tasks.contextSummary: A car accelerates with constant driving force; draw a tangent at 20 s.
solutionStructure: Draw a local tangent at 20 s.
Calculate change in velocity / change in time using the tangent.

criteria.rule: Appropriate tangent attempt at the requested point.
Acceleration identified or used as graph gradient.
Official total-score bands: 1.00–1.20 m/s² scores 3 total; narrower 1.05–1.15 scores 4 total. These totals are not extra marks to add.

acceptableAlternatives: Clear gradient working can imply the gradient relationship.
dependencies: Bands are total-score guidance; preserve preceding construction/method context.
Rendering precision matters. Do not reuse these fixed numeric bands for a different generated graph.

commonErrors.description: Using a chord from the origin instead of a tangent
Using velocity at 20 s divided by 20 s as instantaneous acceleration

requiredKnowledge: Distance as area under a positive velocity-time graph
tasks.contextSummary: Estimate distance during the first 80 s of the same car journey.
solutionStructure: Use area between graph and time axis up to 80 s.
Estimate by strips, shapes or grid squares.
Approximate distance 3750 m; precise source acceptance is banded.

criteria.rule: Distance as area stated or evident in working.
Official total-score bands: 3200–4200 m gives 3 total, 3500–4000 gives 4 total, 3700–3800 gives 5 total. Do not add the totals as independent credits.

acceptableAlternatives: Trapezia, rectangles/triangles and counting squares are allowed.
dependencies: Use the graph from page 30; the page 31 prompt alone is insufficient.
The native 5-mark task cannot be served under the custom even-mark rule without a separately reviewed adaptation.
